body:
What is the bug here? This sounds like a support question or like a missing feature

If the issue is that the `CursorShape.CURSOR_MOVE` and `CursorShape.CURSOR_DRAG` are the same that's [documented](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_input.html#class-input-constant-cursor-drag)

But I don't see how the Mozilla documentation is relevant here, are you exporting for web? But regardless the cursors in Godot aren't bound by the Mozilla documentation

There's no default "closed/open hand" cursors on Windows, so the closest logical equivalent is used, see https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/menurc/about-cursors

Current cursor mapping is:
| Godot Cursor | Windows Cursor |
|---|---|
| CURSOR_ARROW | IDC_ARROW |
| CURSOR_IBEAM | IDC_IBEAM |
| CURSOR_POINTING_HAND | IDC_HAND |
| CURSOR_CROSS | IDC_CROSS |
| CURSOR_WAIT | IDC_WAIT |
| CURSOR_BUSY | IDC_APPSTARTING |
| CURSOR_DRAG | IDC_SIZEALL |
| CURSOR_CAN_DROP | IDC_ARROW |
| CURSOR_FORBIDDEN | IDC_NO |
| CURSOR_VSIZE | IDC_SIZENS |
| CURSOR_HSIZE | IDC_SIZEWE |
| CURSOR_BDIAGSIZE | IDC_SIZENESW |
| CURSOR_FDIAGSIZE | IDC_SIZENWSE |
| CURSOR_MOVE | IDC_SIZEALL |
| CURSOR_VSPLIT | IDC_SIZENS |
| CURSOR_HSPLIT | IDC_SIZEWE |
| CURSOR_HELP | IDC_HELP |

If you need one, you should use a custom cursor.

We probably can include custom cursors with the engine, but these won't match the current Windows theme, so not sure if we should.

For the reference, here's all platform mappings, with missing unique cursors marked:

| Godot Cursor | Windows | X11 | Wayland | macOS | Web | Android |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CURSOR_ARROW | IDC_ARROW | left_ptr | SHAPE_DEFAULT | arrowCursor | "default" | TYPE_DEFAULT |
| CURSOR_IBEAM | IDC_IBEAM | xterm | SHAPE_TEXT | BeamCursor | "text" | TYPE_TEXT |
| CURSOR_POINTING_HAND | IDC_HAND | hand2 | SHAPE_POINTER | pointingHandCursor | "pointer" | TYPE_HAND |
| CURSOR_CROSS | IDC_CROSS | cross | SHAPE_CROSSHAIR | crosshairCursor | "crosshair" | TYPE_CROSSHAIR |
| CURSOR_WAIT | IDC_WAIT | watch | SHAPE_WAIT | arrowCursor ❌ | "wait" | TYPE_WAIT |
| CURSOR_BUSY | IDC_APPSTARTING | left_ptr_watch | SHAPE_PROGRESS | arrowCursor ❌ | "progress" | TYPE_WAIT ❌ |
| CURSOR_DRAG | IDC_SIZEALL ❌ | fleur | SHAPE_GRAB | closedHandCursor | "grab" | TYPE_GRABBING |
| CURSOR_CAN_DROP | IDC_ARROW ❌ | dnd-move | SHAPE_GRABBING | openHandCursor | "grabbing" | TYPE_GRABBING ❌ |
| CURSOR_FORBIDDEN | IDC_NO | crossed_circle | SHAPE_NO_DROP | operationNotAllowedCursor | "no-drop" | TYPE_DEFAULT ❌ |
| CURSOR_VSIZE | IDC_SIZENS | v_double_arrow | SHAPE_NS_RESIZE | windowResizeNorthSouthCursor | "ns-resize" | TYPE_VERTICAL_DOUBLE_ARROW |
| CURSOR_HSIZE | IDC_SIZEWE | h_double_arrow | SHAPE_EW_RESIZE | windowResizeEastWestCursor | "ew-resize" | TYPE_HORIZONTAL_DOUBLE_ARROW |
| CURSOR_BDIAGSIZE | IDC_SIZENESW | size_bdiag | SHAPE_NESW_RESIZE | windowResizeNorthEastSouthWestCursor | "nesw-resize" | TYPE_TOP_LEFT_DIAGONAL_DOUBLE_ARROW |
| CURSOR_FDIAGSIZE | IDC_SIZENWSE | size_fdiag | SHAPE_NWSE_RESIZE | windowResizeNorthWestSouthEastCursor | "nwse-resize" | TYPE_TOP_RIGHT_DIAGONAL_DOUBLE_ARROW |
| CURSOR_MOVE | IDC_SIZEALL | move | SHAPE_MOVE | arrowCursor ❌ | "move" | TYPE_GRAB |
| CURSOR_VSPLIT | IDC_SIZENS | row_resize | SHAPE_ROW_RESIZE | resizeUpDownCursor | "row-resize" | TYPE_VERTICAL_DOUBLE_ARROW ❌ |
| CURSOR_HSPLIT | IDC_SIZEWE | col_resize | SHAPE_COL_RESIZE | resizeLeftRightCursor | "col-resize" | TYPE_HORIZONTAL_DOUBLE_ARROW ❌ |
| CURSOR_HELP | IDC_HELP | question_arrow | SHAPE_HELP | helpCursor | "help" | TYPE_HELP |

There's no cursor shape support on iOS at all.

> If the issue is that the CursorShape.CURSOR_MOVE and CursorShape.CURSOR_DRAG are the same that's [documented](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_input.html#class-input-constant-cursor-drag) At least if it's documented then it's not a bug. I thought it was because it wasn't in the docs inside my 4.5.1 installation: > There's no default "closed/open hand" cursors on Windows I thought the one used in the CSS spec was from the Windows system images but seems they're provided by the browser. Firefox and Edge have different sprites for these. Thanks for informing me o7. Should this thread be closed? My search now will be how to add my own cursor images to make my own grab sprites I guess.
I think I see how to make custom cursor follow size and color, so if it's works as I suspect, I'll make PR to use built-in cursors for these.
